docs.title: Build a decision. Test it. Release it.
docs.text:
SrotaX evaluates one request document against a Decision Table, Decision Tree, or Flow and returns a result. Start with a shipping policy you can test in Studio and call from Java.

Build your first shipping decision

docs.title: Choose your task
docs.text: I want to… Start here Define request and response fields Data Contracts Reuse an object structure Models Write ordered business rules Decision Tables Route through conditions Decision Trees Transform lists and call decisions Flows Share and deploy changes Change sets, then Releases Call a released decision from Java Java integration Check expression support Operator reference

docs.title: Understand the lifecycle
docs.text:
Change set → Save draft → Test → Merge into Main → Create release → Activate environment → Execute.

A successful draft test does not deploy a decision. A merge does not activate a release. Runtime calls use the release active in the API key's environment.

This documentation describes the locally verified implementation. See verification and boundaries, including what has not been certified against MongoDB.

docs.title: Build a shipping decision
docs.text:
Create a policy that charges 9 below a subtotal of 100 and offers free shipping at 100 or above. Both rules return the shipping method Standard.

You need an accessible workspace, permission to edit assets, and permission to release/activate and create an API key for the final integration steps. Ask your workspace administrator if these actions are unavailable.

docs.title: 1. Start a change set
docs.text: Open Change Sets, create a change set named Shipping quickstart, and select it in the workspace header. Main is read-only. In Catalog, choose New Asset, enter Shipping quickstart, and choose Decision Table.

docs.title: 2. Define the contract
docs.text:
Open Data Contract. Under Inputs, expand input and add:

Name Type Required Example subtotal Number Yes 75

Under Outputs, add:

Name Type Required Example fee Number Yes 9 method String Yes Standard

The payload is {"subtotal":75}, not {"input":{"subtotal":75}}. The input. prefix identifies a field inside Studio; it is not an extra envelope your caller supplies.

docs.title: 3. Define two rules
docs.text:
Open Design. Add a condition column for input.subtotal and result columns for output.fee and output.method. Enter the rows in this order:

Row Order subtotal Shipping fee Shipping method 1 Greater than or equal to ($gte) 100 Fixed value 0 Fixed value Standard 2 Less than ($lt) 100 Fixed value 9 Fixed value Standard

The table returns the first matching row. These conditions do not overlap and cover numeric subtotals. This example does not reject negative amounts; add an explicit business rule if that is required.

docs.title: 4. Test boundary values
docs.text:
Open Test Panel → Test Input, enter the JSON below, and choose Run Test:

{"subtotal":75}

Result should contain:

{"fee":9,"method":"Standard"}

Trace identifies row 2 as matched. Also test 0, 99.99, 100, and 150. Subtotals 0, 75, and 99.99 charge 9; 100 and 150 charge 0. Test {"subtotal":"wrong"} and confirm a validation failure. On a change set, testing includes unsaved editor changes.

docs.title: 5. Save and merge
docs.text: Choose Save Draft, then Validate. Open the change set's comparison, check that only your intended rules and contract changed, and merge into Main. Resolve any content conflicts before merging. The asset now has an immutable published version; this is not yet a deployment.

docs.title: 6. Create and activate a release
docs.text:
Open Releases on Main and create a release from its current revision. A release includes the whole workspace Main snapshot, not just this table. For your first walkthrough, use a dedicated workspace or review everything included.

Activate the release in Development. Activation selects the complete release for that environment. It does not change Production.

docs.title: 7. Call it from Java
docs.text: Create a Development API key, copy the asset ID from the asset's API integration information, and run the Java example. Keep the key server-side. The runtime returns an envelope; check success before reading data.

docs.title: Reproducible example
docs.text:
The repository includes examples/shipping/authoring.json and five cases in examples/shipping/cases.json. The automated walkthrough uses real management and runtime HTTP APIs against a disposable database; verification records its scope.

Download the authoring JSON and test cases. The authoring file is for API/fixture use; it is not a claim that Studio has a whole-asset JSON import button.

docs.title: Verification and boundaries
docs.text: This documentation was built against the current local SrotaX code and running services on 2026-10-23/24. The source repositories contain uncommitted work, so a Git commit alone does not identify this exact build. File fingerprints and the operator catalog snapshot are recorded under verification/ and reference/.

docs.title: Shipping journey
docs.text:
scripts/verify-journey.mjs ran against a disposable PostgreSQL database with fixture identity and real Management and Runtime HTTP servers. It verified creation, schema persistence, validation, five preview cases, merge, immutable version retrieval, release creation, activation, five runtime cases, release-linked history, wrong-type failures, invalid-key denial, and the Java HTTP client.

Fixture authentication is test-only. This does not test Google/Microsoft identity providers, production infrastructure, or a customer's permissions configuration. No existing customer release was activated or overwritten.

Browser verification additionally loaded the published table and contract, generated example input, ran the test successfully, confirmed Row 2 matched, and checked Development activation. The quickstart screenshots come from this disposable workspace. Creation, merge, and activation were exercised through HTTP, not by clicking every Studio action.

docs.title: Operator reference
docs.text:
The reference is generated from the actual Management operator catalog. Metadata reports compatibility classifications, source revision, null/missing behavior, signatures, and limitations. These are attributed as engine metadata, not independently certified MongoDB equivalence.

The suite has 23 successful compiler/engine examples and one reproduced known failure.

Selected runnable expression examples are checked against the compiler and engine by scripts/verify-expressions.sh. They do not certify every registered operator or every BSON type. A full MongoDB differential suite remains separate work; the documentation does not claim it has passed.

docs.title: Build checks
docs.text: Local Markdown links and JSON examples are checked by scripts/check.py. MkDocs strict build validates navigation. The CI workflow repeats these checks; the fixture journey requires a sibling backend build and is documented separately.

docs.title: Known gaps surfaced
docs.text:
• A literal-array $size expression compiled but failed during execution ($size requires one argument). Its operator page and regression fixture record this limitation.
  • Older backend ad-hoc E2E scripts still contain tuple-shaped input fixtures. This new walkthrough uses nested schemas and does not reuse those obsolete payloads.
  • Runtime OpenAPI currently has a generic response schema rather than an exhaustive typed failure contract.
  • Direct Java embedding and broad MongoDB semantic parity are not certified by this documentation.

docs.title: Call SrotaX from Java
docs.text: Use Java's HTTP client to execute a decision through the Runtime API. This approach does not embed the engine or require a SrotaX SDK.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Merge the decision, create a release, activate it in the API key's environment, and obtain that environment's key. Use the decision's stable ID, not its display name. Set these environment variables through your deployment's secret configuration:

  • SROTAX_RUNTIME_URL: runtime origin, for example https://runtime.example.com.
  • SROTAX_DECISION_ID: decision UUID.
  • SROTAX_API_KEY: runtime key. Do not put it in frontend code or source control.

The repository's examples/java/ShippingClient.java works on Java 17+ and was executed with Java 21 against the disposable runtime.

java examples/java/ShippingClient.java

The sample sends {"subtotal":75} and prints the JSON response. It checks HTTP status; your application must also parse the response using its JSON library and check success == true before using data. For the shipping example, data is {"fee":9,"method":"Standard"}.

Download ShippingClient.java

import java.net.URI;
import java.net.http.*;
import java.time.Duration;

/** Java 17+; API key stays in the environment. The response is a JSON envelope. */
public class ShippingClient {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        String base = required("SROTAX_RUNTIME_URL").replaceAll("/$", "");
        String decision = required("SROTAX_DECISION_ID");
        var client = HttpClient.newBuilder().connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5)).build();
        var request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI.create(base + "/api/runtime/decisions/" + decision + "/execute"))
            .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30))
            .header("Authorization", "Bearer " + required("SROTAX_API_KEY"))
            .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
            .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("{\"subtotal\":75}"))
            .build();
        var response = client.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString());
        if (response.statusCode() != 200) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("SrotaX HTTP status " + response.statusCode());
        }
        // The calling application must also parse and check `success` before using `data`.
        System.out.println(response.body());
    }
    private static String required(String name) {
        String value = System.getenv(name);
        if (value == null || value.isBlank()) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Missing " + name);
        return value;
    }
}

docs.title: Handle failures
docs.text:
A transport failure or timeout is not a business result. An HTTP 200 response may still describe a failed execution. Keep these paths distinct. See Runtime API.

The sample uses a 5-second connection timeout and 30-second request timeout as example client settings; these do not configure server limits. Choose them based on your deployment. Do not blindly retry a Flow containing external side effects: a timeout does not prove it never ran.

docs.title: Embedding is a separate integration
docs.text: This guide verifies remote execution only. Direct JVM engine embedding does not automatically provide SrotaX release loading, workspace permissions, API-key scope, reference data, or dependency resolution. A supported embedding contract needs separate verification before it belongs in this guide.

docs.title: Runtime API
docs.text:
Send one JSON document to:

POST /api/runtime/decisions/{decisionId}/execute
Authorization: Bearer <runtime-api-key>
Content-Type: application/json

The key determines organisation, workspace, and environment. Do not send those as body fields to select another scope. The request body is the decision's input document.

docs.title: Successful execution
docs.text: The response includes success, data, and execution metadata such as runId. Check success before using data; preserve runId for troubleshooting. Do not assume every HTTP 200 is a successful decision evaluation.

docs.text:

These cases are verified by the documentation walkthrough. Other limits and error details are deployment-specific; do not treat this table as an exhaustive HTTP error schema.

docs.title: Expressions and conditions
docs.text:
Visual expressions choose a supported function and supply its arguments. Advanced JSON expressions use the engine's expression syntax. The modes contain separate expressions: select the one you intend to use. They are not automatically synchronized.

input.*, local.*, output.*, and the current list item have different scopes. Select fields from the picker where possible. A reference that exists in another step or another asset is not automatically available at the current location.

The operator inventory separates registered engine operators from functions offered to the Visual editor. Scoped operators such as $map, $filter, and $reduce require scope-aware configuration and are not generic Visual function entries.

Condition pickers also contain business-facing recipes built from one or more operators. A recipe name does not necessarily identify a MongoDB operator. Use condition reference to inspect their metadata.

For each expression, test its normal value, null/missing inputs, wrong types, and boundary values relevant to your contract. Structural validation cannot establish that the formula is your intended business rule.

docs.title: Supported schema format
docs.text:
Models and contract sections use nested OpenAPI-style Schema Objects. The supported subset is intentionally narrower than unrestricted OpenAPI or JSON Schema.

{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "subtotal": {"type": "number", "example": 75},
    "customer": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}},
      "required": ["name"]
    },
    "items": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
  },
  "required": ["subtotal"]
}
Feature Supported representation Object type: object, properties, optional required array Scalar string, number, boolean Date/time type: string, format: date-time List type: array, items schema; {} permits unspecified item type Metadata title, description, example where accepted Model reference $ref: #/components/schemas/{modelId}

Stored refs use model UUIDs, not names. OpenAPI import/export converts readable external component names at the boundary. $ref objects cannot add sibling custom fields. Examples must match scalar types.

Unsupported keywords are rejected, including unrestricted oneOf, allOf, anyOf, enum, validation constraints such as minimum, and arbitrary additionalProperties. Use a decision or validation step for business constraints supported by the editor. integer is not a separate accepted scalar type here; use number.

Property names must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*. The current parser enforces a 64-field limit and nesting checks; model resolution also checks expanded references and cycles. Do not use recursive schemas.

This page is derived from srotax-core/SchemaContracts.java and model resolution, not a claim of full OpenAPI conformance.

docs.title: Flow step reference
docs.text:
Configure steps using available contract fields and compatible local destinations. This is a task reference for Studio operations; it is not a promise that every MongoDB aggregation stage is exposed.

Step Purpose Important configuration Request Start with the incoming document Input contract Validate Data Check required values and types Fields to validate and behavior Set Fields Assign fixed values, copies, or expressions Destination and source/expression; never write input.* Choose Fields Select the fields retained in a working/result object Source and retained fields; input remains immutable Transform Each Item Map list items Source list, item expression/mapping, destination Filter List Keep matching items Source list, item conditions, destination Flatten List Flatten nested lists Source and destination Sort List Order list items Sort fields/directions; in-place only for local lists Trim List Keep a range or count Source, range/count, destination Aggregate List Calculate a list summary List, operation, value field, destination Check Exists Test whether matching items exist List, predicate, boolean destination Lookup Read reference-data values Dataset/version, key mapping, result destination If / Else Route by conditions Conditions and complete outgoing branches Decision Table / Decision Tree Call a decision asset Dependency, input mappings, result destination Call Flow Call a reusable Flow Dependency, input mappings, result destination Response Return the chosen response Response mapping/shape compatible with Outputs

Do not infer support for collection-level stages such as $merge or $out from MongoDB documentation. Use the editor's actual palette and validate the completed Flow. Operator registration alone does not establish that a stage is available in Studio.

docs.title: Organize the Catalog
docs.text:
Group assets by business purpose, such as Orders / Shipping, Orders / Fulfillment, and Pricing. Nested folders are supported. Assets is the root location.

Open a folder to see its immediate contents, and use breadcrumbs to return to a parent. Workspace search helps locate assets and folders across the hierarchy. Asset identity is an ID; moving an asset does not change its references or executable content.

Create, rename, or move folders inside an editable change set. Only empty folders can be deleted; assets outside the current editing view can still make a folder nonempty. Deletion is also checked by the server.

Untouched folders reflect Main. Your folder edits stay in the selected change set until merged. A folder-only merge changes organization without creating new executable asset versions.

docs.title: Work in a change set
docs.text:
Main is the shared integrated state and is read-only in the editors. A change set stores your touched drafts and organizational edits until merge.

  1. Create and select a change set.
  2. Edit and Save Draft for each intended asset or model.
  3. Test and validate.
  4. Inspect the comparison against Main.
  5. Resolve content conflicts, then merge.

Merge validates and creates immutable versions of changed executable assets. Shared model changes can also require revalidation and recompilation of consumers. Failed validation must be fixed before merge succeeds.

docs.title: Understand isolation
docs.text:
A change set does not copy every asset and folder when it is created. It stores overrides for touched resources. Untouched folders follow later Main merges; your unmerged folder edits remain private. Do not treat a change set as a fully frozen copy of the workspace.

Folder structure changes do not present content-conflict resolution; the merge applies recorded organizational edits with structural validation. Asset and model content conflicts still require resolution. See Catalog.

docs.title: Save, merge, release, activate
docs.text:
Action Effect Save Draft Persists editable work in the change set Merge Integrates changes into Main and creates immutable resource versions Create release Captures the complete Main revision Activate Selects a release for an environment's runtime calls

Do not use “published version” as a synonym for “currently running in Production.”

docs.title: Define a Data Contract
docs.text:
A contract declares the shape and types of the values your decision accepts and returns. Define it before adding condition columns or mapping fields.

Section Studio path Purpose Inputs input.subtotal Incoming request; immutable in Flows Local (Flows) local.items Intermediate values that steps may replace Outputs output.fee Declared response fields

docs.title: Edit fields
docs.text:
Select a section, expand its root row, and use + to add a field. Set its name, type, Required checkbox, example, and optional description. Objects contain child fields; lists declare an item type. Object lists can contain nested fields or refer to a Model.

Required means the value must be supplied where validated. An example helps construct test input; it is not a default value and does not populate missing production input.

docs.title: Switch between Fields and JSON
docs.text:
Both views edit the same schema. Switching from JSON to Fields validates and applies valid JSON automatically. If it is invalid, stay in JSON, fix the displayed errors, and switch again. There is no separate Apply to Fields action.

The editor uses input, local, and output sections. The authoring API uses contract.inputs, contract.variables, and contract.outputs. Each section is a nested schema object, not positional field arrays. See schema reference.

docs.title: Use a Model
docs.text:
Choose a model in the root or object row's Type area. Its fields appear as a read-only preview. Choosing a model replaces custom descendants under that object. Adding a manual child clears the model binding; detaching removes the reference and its displayed descendants. Neither action is a safe way to keep a copied snapshot of the model fields.

References follow the current model in the selected change set. See Models before changing a shared definition.

docs.title: Build a Flow
docs.text: Use a Flow to transform one request, call reusable decisions, branch, and return a response. It is not a collection ETL pipeline.

docs.title: Keep the original input
docs.text:
input.* is immutable. Read from it and write working values into local.*. Reuse a local variable when its previous value is no longer needed. For example:

  1. Transform input.items into local.items.
  2. Filter or sort local.items in place.
  3. Aggregate local.items into a local total.
  4. Assign the result to an output field.

You do not need originalInput: the original request remains in input.*. In-place list operations must target a compatible local list. Set Fields and Choose Fields must not modify the input namespace.

docs.title: Configure each step
docs.text:
Select a step to open its drawer. Choose source fields, output destination, and operation-specific options. Field choices depend on the contract and preceding steps. An expression's current item is scoped to its list operation; it is not a workspace variable.

When calling a Table, Tree, or Flow, map the called asset's input fields from available sources and map its result into the caller. Review dependency selection before merging; a published dependency and a same-change-set draft are different choices.

docs.title: Branch and return
docs.text:
Give each branch a complete route to a Response. Current graph editing permits one incoming connection per step; branches do not merge into a shared downstream step. Validate disconnected paths and test both sides of conditions.

Use the Test Panel's trace to inspect ordered steps and nested calls. The canvas highlights the executed path. See the step reference for the supported operations.

docs.title: Reuse Models
docs.text: A Model is a named object schema in a workspace. Use it when multiple contracts or nested objects share a structure, such as an Address. Models have a flat namespace; there are no model packages in this version.

docs.title: Create and reference
docs.text:
1. Select an editable change set and open Models.
  2. Create a model, give it a name, and define its fields using Fields or JSON.
  3. Save the model draft.
  4. Open an asset's Data Contract and choose the model on an object row or as the item schema of an object list.

Studio and Models use the same field editor. Referenced children are shown for inspection, not copied into the consuming contract's authoring definition.

docs.title: When a model changes
docs.text:
Consumers resolve the current model in their selected change set, falling back to Main when it has not been edited there. The editor refreshes referenced fields on focus and periodically while a change-set editor is active; this is not instant collaborative streaming.

Merging a model change validates and recompiles affected Main consumers. A field removal or incompatible type change can block the merge until its consuming rules are fixed. Existing executable versions and releases retain their resolved model definitions.

There is no Update from model button or user-facing version selector. Internal immutable revisions still exist for reproducibility.

docs.title: Import OpenAPI components
docs.text:
Open the import dialog, supply an OpenAPI document, select component schemas with the checkboxes (or Select all), and import the selected models. The eye icon previews a schema. Select every referenced component that is not already available under a matching name.

If matching names exist, Overwrite existing models replaces their fields and description inside the current change set while preserving their IDs. Review consumers before merging. Import is atomic: unsupported keywords, missing references, or cycles reject the operation.

Import translates component names into stable model-ID $ref values. Export translates those IDs back to readable component names in one OpenAPI document. Renaming a model therefore does not change its consumers' stored references.

Only the supported schema subset is accepted; “OpenAPI import” does not mean all OpenAPI schema features are supported.

docs.title: Release and activate
docs.text:
A release is an immutable snapshot of one complete workspace Main revision. Merge your change set before creating it. Creating again for the same Main revision returns the existing release.

Review all included assets and dependencies. A release is not a selected subset of just the Flow you were editing. It captures the exact compiled definitions and model snapshots used by its assets.

docs.title: Activate an environment
docs.text:
Development and Production each select one release. Activation replaces the environment's active release atomically. Runtime API keys are scoped to an environment, so the same decision ID may produce different results in Development and Production.

Creating a release alone does not activate it. An asset unavailable in the environment's active release cannot be executed there.

docs.title: Roll back
docs.text:
Activate a previous release for that environment. Rollback switches the complete snapshot; it does not selectively undo one asset. To combine an older rule with newer unrelated rules, author the desired combination in a change set, merge, and create a new release.

Main and existing releases are not edited by activation. Requests already executing use the release snapshot they resolved for that invocation.

docs.title: Write a Decision Table
docs.text: Use a table when business rules fit rows of conditions and results. Define Inputs and Outputs in Data Contract first, then choose those fields when adding columns.

docs.title: Evaluation order matters
docs.text:
Rows run top-to-bottom. The first matching row supplies the result. A rule subtotal < 50 placed below subtotal < 100 cannot win for a subtotal of 25: the broader earlier row already matches. Put the more specific rule first or make the conditions disjoint.

Result cells can assign values or use the supported editing modes. Choose types that match the output contract. Do not rely on JSON strings being silently converted into numbers at runtime.

docs.title: Inspect and test
docs.text:
Use the shared Test Panel. Result shows output, Trace identifies the matched row, and Issues explains failures. Test each rule and exact thresholds, plus missing and wrong-type inputs. See the shipping walkthrough.

On Main, adding rows and columns is disabled. Search remains available for inspection. Select an editable change set to change the table. Save Draft persists editor changes; Run Test in a change set includes unsaved changes.

docs.title: Test decisions
docs.text:
The same Test Panel is used by Tables, Trees, and Flows; its contents adapt to the asset.

Tab Use it for Test Input Enter a JSON request and run it Result Inspect the returned output Trace Inspect the matched table row, tree path, or Flow execution steps Issues Read validation and execution failures

Use example input as a starting point, then edit it to test boundary values. Examples are not a coverage guarantee.

On Main, the label beside Run Test identifies the version being executed. In a change set, the test uses the current draft, including unsaved changes. Saving after a test is still necessary to persist the draft.

docs.title: Minimum test set
docs.text:
Test a normal case, each condition boundary, every branch or row you expect to reach, missing required fields, incorrect types, and empty lists where relevant. For Models, repeat affected tests after changing a shared field.

A green validation result proves structural acceptance, not that the rule matches business intent. A valid but shadowed table row can still produce the wrong business outcome.

docs.title: Build a Decision Tree
docs.text:
Use a tree when decisions are naturally expressed as branches. Begin with the start node, add conditions, connect each outcome to a result or another condition, and define the returned output fields on result nodes.

For a shipping example, branch on input.subtotal >= 100: the yes result returns fee 0, and the no result returns fee 9. Both return method Standard.

Test one input for every result leaf, including exact thresholds. Use Result to verify returned values and Trace to inspect execution. The graph indicates the executed path; do not interpret tile colour alone as evidence of execution.

On Main, graph zoom and navigation remain available. Adding conditions or results requires an editable change set. A missing branch or invalid output is a validation problem, not an instruction for the runtime to invent a result.
